requirements.text: Validate schema and quarantine ambiguous identity without guessing.
Bind approval to an immutable entity/revision and serialize accepted revisions.
Deduplicate events and retain decision provenance through retries.

problem.scope: Deidentified authored records exercise schema validation, identity resolution, ordered approval and idempotent commit. This is an ingestion pattern with no patient data, clinical rules or clinical decisions.

provenance.note: Authored interview preparation. Technical references support mechanisms, not the claim that a company asked this question.

references.supports: Transactions isolate concurrent authorization and mutation decisions; retries remain explicit.

stages.explanation: Validate schema and quarantine ambiguous identity without guessing. [Data ingestion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_integration) moves source records into a usable destination. Stable source identity and progress records distinguish genuinely new data from repeated delivery or a restarted import. Consider this case: Approval names revision 2 hash A. Submit revision 2 hash B or revision 1 after revision 2 commits.
invariants: Validate schema and quarantine ambiguous identity without guessing.

stages.explanation: Validate event envelopes before accepting workflow intent. Own immutable raw event hashes and revision state. event receipt identity belongs to Ingest coordinator; event IDs and states belongs to Staging ledger. [Immutable data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immutable_object) is built as a complete new value rather than changed underneath readers. Publishing one reference lets each reader keep a consistent version.
invariants: event receipt identity belongs to Ingest coordinator; event IDs and states belongs to Staging ledger.

[A transaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database_transaction) commits related state changes together or leaves them unapplied. The database must enforce the relevant condition during the write, rather than trusting an earlier read. Consider this case: Approval names revision 2 hash A. stages.explanation: Uniquely admit event ID and detect the same ID with conflicting bytes. Conflicting reuse of an event ID is an error. [Collaborative editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operational_transformation) must reconcile concurrent edits against an agreed document version. Sending changes is only one part; reconnects also need a way to recover missing updates and conflicts. Consider this case: Approval names revision 2 hash A.
invariants: Conflicting reuse of an event ID is an error.
